role: smallest default coding-agent skill/harness configuration for solo ABVX development
baseline: native Codex with ABVX-OS AGENTS.md and task prompt
candidate: native, Matt Pocock selected skills, Addy Osmani selected skills, and Ponytail ON/OFF
recommendation: Do not install or promote any external skill pack yet. Retain Native Codex as the provisional default; repeat the same fixtures with a reproducible model-agent execution adapter before selecting external skills. Treat Ponytail as a selective review intervention candidate, not an always-on default, until quality is measured.

qualitative_assessment.execution_limit: The local harness can execute deterministic fixture tests but has no reproducible model-agent adapter, so generated correctness, changed LOC, retries, human review burden, and actual token usage remain unobserved.
qualitative_assessment.matt_qualification: MIT, active at observed commit, plain-file/Codex-compatible through npx skills installer; selected TDD, diagnosing-bugs, and code-review because they map directly to the three fixtures. Setup also asks for repository configuration, which is outside the smallest default.
qualitative_assessment.addy_qualification: MIT, active at observed commit, native Codex plugin path; selected test-driven-development, incremental-implementation, and code-review-and-quality. The inspected selected text is materially larger and the pack exposes broader lifecycle commands than this bakeoff needs.
qualitative_assessment.ponytail_qualification: MIT, active at observed commit, Codex plugin with lifecycle hooks and default full mode. Its reuse/stdlib/YAGNI rule is relevant, but hooks and always-on injection add operational coupling; test selectively before default-on adoption.
qualitative_assessment.compatibility: All sources conflict with no explicit ABVX rule in the inspected subset, but external setup conventions, hooks, lifecycle stages, and issue-tracker assumptions must not override AGENTS.md or local-first boundaries.
qualitative_assessment.ceremony: Native has no extra setup or stages. Matt selected adds 2 setup commands and 2 stages; Addy adds 2 setup commands and 3 stages; Ponytail adds 2 setup commands plus hook/restart handling and 1 stage. These are footprint observations, not agent outcome measurements.

risks: No model-agent execution means external quality ranking is unproven
Static skill byte counts are context proxies, not token counts
Ponytail lifecycle hooks may widen operational scope
Matt setup may introduce issue-tracker/document conventions
Addy exposes a broad 24-skill lifecycle pack even when only three skills are selected
unresolved_questions: Which configuration produces the smallest correct diff under the same real Codex model and prompt?
Does Ponytail reduce unnecessary LOC without increasing regressions or review burden?
What is the actual token/context cost in Codex desktop?
Should any selected skill be referenced rather than installed?
